prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas, and has shoulder injury. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1399; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you were involved in in Baytown, Texas. Do you understand that this call is being recorded?

A: Yes, I understand.

Q: Please state your full name and the best number to reach you.

A: [Claimant name and phone on file], I think you already have those.

Q: That's fine, we'll confirm them later. Can you walk me through what happened?

A: I was driving on a two-lane road heading toward the shopping center. The other car came toward me from the opposite direction and drifted into my lane. We hit nearly head-on, but it was slow. I'd say maybe ten or fifteen miles an hour.

Q: Were you able to stop, or did the impact happen before you could react?

A: I braked, but there wasn't time to avoid it. The airbags did not deploy, and I stayed in my seat.

Q: Did you feel any pain right after the collision?

A: Not right away. About an hour later my right shoulder started aching, and by the next morning I could barely lift my arm above my shoulder.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or other medical provider since the accident?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic the same week. They took X-rays and told me it looked like a strain. I'm now doing physical therapy twice a week.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt at the time?

A: Yes, I was.

Q: Is there anything you think I should know that we haven't covered?

A: Only that I'm still having trouble sleeping on that side. I'd like to get this resolved so I can get back to work normally.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
